idiom: hit the nail on the head
meaning: to describe exactly the cause of a problem or the exact truth of a situation
example: You hit the nail on the head when you said the team lacks clear goals.
origin: Probably from carpentry, where a precise strike drives the nail in exactly and efficiently

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hammer something into a wall
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is a literal misreading; the idiom has nothing to do with physical hammering

wrong_meanings.meaning: to make a mistake while building something
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes accuracy in understanding, not a construction error

wrong_meanings.meaning: to give up on a project completely
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom refers to identifying the right point, not abandoning an effort

explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' means to identify exactly the right point or cause. It is useful at B2 level for discussing opinions and explaining why an argument is accurate.
